utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Madam Registrar, good morning to you. And good morning, everybody. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours and everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Madam. Now, let's start from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I should have waited a bit more. He's just entered the courtroom now. So there is nothing else to say in that regard. All the accused are present here. From the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Bourgon and Mr. Haynes. The Prosecution today, it's Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Nicholls, Mr. Vanderpuye, and Mr. Elderkin. So we need to go through the exhibits relating to yesterday's witness. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We have no exhibits for this witness. All our exhibits were tendered through Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, merci. Mr. Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Miletic's Defence would like to tender documents 5D1181, 5D1182, 5D1186, 5D1187, all to be marked for identification, and we would also like to tender for admission 5DIC 206. I believe that I've given you the right number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrusic. Any objections, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections from any of the other Defence teams? So these are being marked for identification purposes for the time being pending translation following which they will be fully admitted. That's it. So yes, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I actually have some documents I'd like to tender in relation to the witness's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- cross-examination. We submitted a tender list. I think everybody has it. I'm not sure if the Court has it. You do have it, okay. So there is just 65 ter 2821, 2823, 3407, 3412, 3413, 3424 and 3425.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection from any of the other Defence teams? None. They are so admitted, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that concludes Mr. Blagojevic's testimony. And we can start now with the next witness, who is Branko Bogicevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bogicevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I welcome you. You've been summoned as a witness by the accused Colonel Popovic, Vujadin Popovic, and before you start your testimony, you're requested under our rules to make a solemn declaration that you will be testifying the truth. The text is going to be handed to you now by Madam Usher. Please read the text out loud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable. You are first going to be asked a series of questions by counsel for Colonel Popovic and then we see who else wishes to cross-examine you. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bogicevic.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, would you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Branko Bogicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me the year and the place of your birth?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: 1952, on 20th of June, in Djevanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What municipality is that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What is your profession, please?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm a retired driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in the war? Were you mobilised during the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when, during what period of time?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Between the 20th of July, to the end. Actually, the 22nd of July 1992, to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have a rank?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you a foot soldier?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was a foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do during the war?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: All the time I was just driving.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In what unit?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: The Zvornik Brigade, the logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: There were a few of them. And the last one was Radivoje Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether it was him or somebody else that you received your tasks from, your orders?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Radisav Pantic was the one who gave me orders. He was in charge of us drivers. He was the official in charge of transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "For us drivers" --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I mean the technical services, both the drivers and the mechanics.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to show you a travel work order dating back to July 1995. This is Prosecution Exhibit 215 -- 295, and the page number is 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection, and I apologise for interrupting. I just wanted to tell Your Honours this is a document where a revised translation has been passed out to you. There is a small logistics issue with this exhibit. The reason is it is already in e-court. However, the English translation in e-court had several illegibles written on it and we have revised the translation. It's been passed out to all counsel and I think Mr. Zivanovic agrees with me on this. We have a better English translation now. But for reasons I don't fully understand it was impossible to put it into e-court at this time since it's already there under a different translation so what we were told is to use the English translation on the ELMO, if necessary, and then we would give this another number. I'm sorry to object, to stand up, but that's where we are now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not at all. As far as the witness is concerned, he can still see the original document in his own language on e-court. As far as the rest of us who don't understand the language is concerned, we will do as suggested, we'll put the revised translation document on the ELMO. So Madam Usher, I think you can proceed to put it on the ELMO because I understand that questions are going to be put on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go to page 11, please. Mr. Bogicevic, do you have the document on the screen? The vehicle work log.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see what period is covered in this document? Maybe the last digit is not really very legible. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, no objection. Just if it helps, we do have the original of this document if my friend decides he wants to use it, he's talking about legibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Not necessary if we can agree it's July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally for your information, both of you, we are not broadcasting this because I'm informed the document is confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it is not confidential. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what Madam Registrar told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you verify if it's confidential or not, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I will, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are checking again. In the meantime we will proceed without broadcasting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I believe it is not confidential, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, let's proceed. Let's not waste time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see -- or, rather, would you read the type of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It's TAM 80.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the same document, can you see your name?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether this vehicle was the one that you drove during the relevant period of time, i.e. in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us a brief description of the vehicle? What kind of a vehicle was that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It is a small lorry with a carrying capacity of 2.5 tonnes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you look at this first page that is in front of you, can you please tell me whether you were supposed to fill in something on the first page or not?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't supposed to fill in anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who it was who was supposed to fill out the first page? Who was supposed to enter all the data that you see on the first page?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It would be the official in charge of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that in the lower part of the page that you have in front of you, there is a box with dates and fuel? Could you please tell me who it was who entered the dates and the fuel that you see entered in here?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: The same official who actually gives you the order to travel somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where you were provided with the fuel when you were supposed to travel somewhere?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Either in the barracks or at the gas station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where was the gas station?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Not far from the barracks, maybe a hundred or 200 metres away from the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the rules were when it came to getting fuel for your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: When the official told you where you were supposed to go, he would take a notepad and write the quantity that you were supposed to get. Then you go to the person who is supposed to give you that fuel, he looks at the notepad and gives you exactly what's written on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Before you were provided with fuel, were you always provided with that written certificate or that little notepad with the figure?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes it was not done in writing. If you were in a haste, if you needed fuel, then the official would call the person providing you with fuel on the phone and that's how it was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were working with that lorry, what would it be that you transported, in very general terms, roughly?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Mostly food for the troops, ammunition as well. We cooperated with the police to bring in troops who were deserting and we would also take troops to the line or back to the barracks. And sometimes, not just sometimes but quite often, we would bring our dead from the line to the hospital and then from the hospital to the place of burial.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also drive our soldiers? If you did, where did you usually drive them to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, when there was a shift changeover, then we would take them from their houses to the line and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also drive some detainees?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have shown you this vehicle work log to ask you this: As a driver, what was your general obligation when it came to the vehicle work log? Were you supposed to have that all the time or not?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Every day you had to make a record of what your duty was and what you accomplished.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What happens when this vehicle work log is full for one month? What happens to it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: You hand it over to the official, and every first day of the month you are provided with a new vehicle work log.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And that's how it was from the beginning of the war, i.e. from the moment you started working as a driver, or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Once you handed the vehicle work log to the official, when a month is over, would you ever have an opportunity to see those vehicle work logs again?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any such opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about this vehicle work log. When was it the first time you saw it after the war, after you had handed it over to the official in 1995, at the end of July?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I saw it last year when you showed it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go to the following page of this document. Can you recognise your handwriting on this page?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We can proceed, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogicevic, I will repeat several questions that you've already answered since they were not entered into the record due to some technical problems. Tell me if you can recognise the handwriting on page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can recognise my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to your handwriting, do you see, and can you indicate, handwriting that is not yours?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, I can recognise the signature by Pantic, Radoslav. I don't recognise the other handwriting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose we need to know which one would that be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate for us which of the signatures we can see here is Pantic's? In other words, can you tell us which one is it looking from the top?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Since he was the man in charge of us, his signature is in the lower, or in the bottom right-hand corner, and then -- it's down there where the stamp should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the bottom right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And when you said third, did you mean third from the top?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: The third, the fifth and the seventh.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The third, the fifth and the seventh looking from the top?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Pantic's signature. I don't recognise the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall who it was who signed these vehicle work logs in addition to Pantic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: There were several individuals who took turns. I don't recall their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you something about a specific entry for the date of the 16th of July. Can you see that? Can you read -- and let's take it step by step. Can you read the hour and the date when you started your trip?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let's just to have as precise a transcript as possible, please. I notice, going through the transcript, that he has not yet indicated with precision his own handwriting on this document. He has indicated Mr. Pantic's but not his.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us once more, aside from the signatures we can see on the right-hand side, who was it who filled out the other columns, such as date, time of start and end of trip, distances, kilometres?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It was I who filled out all of that, all the way through to the kilometres travelled at the far end here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, or, rather, do you recall at all having made this trip on the 16th of July 1995, among other places, also to Pilica?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: If that's what is entered here, it means that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me show you another document now. This is Prosecution Exhibit 291. Do you remember this document? Can you tell us when it was that you saw it for the last time, before coming to The Hague, or I apologise. After 1995, when did you see the document for the first time after 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I saw it last year when you showed it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the very bottom of the document and the right-hand corner. There is a signature there. Can you tell us whose is it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's my signature, and that's how I sign my name in the Cyrillic script.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The text which is written in the Latin script and which says "received by Branko Bogicevic," was it also written by you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: You mean -- what do you mean by me?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I put it awkwardly, I suppose. Did you yourself write the lettering which says, "Received by Branko Bogicevic"?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You saw this document. Can you tell me, was it you who transported fuel pursuant to this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember where the fuel was given into your charge?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the town or the place where you picked the fuel up? What is it that you don't remember, the place where you took charge of the fuel or --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: You asked me whether I had transported the fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Then you must have misunderstood me. My question now is where was it that you took charge of the fuel.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall whether this was in the barracks or at the petrol station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where it was you transported the fuel to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: As it says here, it was taken to Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the amount of fuel you drove to Pilica, if you can?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: 500 litres were taken there and 140 litres were brought back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who ordered you to transport the fuel?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you were a driver in that time period, would you be able to tell us who it could have been who might have given you the order?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Most probably one of the officials, or the desk officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Complain all the time on speculation, and this is nothing but speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's there. Let's proceed. You had no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember in what way the fuel was transported to Pilica? I know that it was trucked there, but what was it -- in what way was it contained?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat his answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Zivanovic, the interpreters didn't catch the witness's answer. Mr. Bogicevic, could you kindly repeat your answer, please, to Mr. Zivanovic's question? The question was: Can you remember in what way the fuel was transported to Pilica? I know that it was trucked there but what was it -- in what way was it contained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Barrels.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall where you got the barrels from?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall whether it was in the barracks or at the petrol station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall it being decanted when you were there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, just when he was where? Is this in Pilica or, I didn't understand the decanted, was this in Zvornik or at the destination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair enough, fair enough. Could you specify this with the witness, please? Your question was: Do you recall it being decanted when were you there? Obviously where?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will repeat my question to make this quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you know, where the barrels were filled with fuel before you were supposed to transport them?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall if this was in the barracks or at the gas station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall if you were given a special document to accompany this particular trip which said where you were supposed to take the fuel to or who it was supposed to be given to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall having been given any such document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You had been working as a driver for a long time, transporting various types of goods, as you said. Can you tell me if it ever happened that you had to make a trip without having the attendant piece of paper telling you who to take the goods to and who it was who was supposed to receive the goods and sign for them?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It would so happen that I would go out into the field transporting foodstuffs without having any sort of document or document. I would deliver the goods and come back. The same went for ammunition. I transported ammunition without any accompanying documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that you were supposed to have documentation as a rule and then it sometimes so happened that you didn't have any documents? Or was it a rule that you wouldn't have any documentation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It would so happen that I would sometimes have documentations and sometimes I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the location where you delivered the fuel at Pilica?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was on the way out of Pilica, in the direction of Bijeljina. There was a small bridge there and a group of soldiers. That was where I pulled over.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were setting out on this trip, did anyone tell you where you were supposed to go and who you were supposed to report to? Did anyone give you any sort of specific instructions?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I was told to go to Pilica. That's what the vehicle work log said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you told to go to that particular spot you've just described for us, or was it described to you in a different way? Can you remember this at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I was told to go to Pilica in the direction of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember -- no, strike that. Were you given the name of a person that you were supposed to contact and deliver the fuel to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who it was that took the fuel over from you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: The soldiers who were waiting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that they were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Our soldiers, they had uniforms, the uniforms of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe the uniforms for us? Were they camouflage uniforms or just regular army uniforms?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please describe the handover of the fuel? The fuel was in the barrels, so how did they go about receiving the fuel from you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: They had a lot of jerrycans, either made of plastic or metal, and there was a hose that we used to decant the fuel from the barrels into the jerrycans.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the hose, was that their hose, your hose?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It was theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And how long did it last, this decanting of the fuel from the barrels into the jerrycans?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: An hour, an hour and a half perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened next? Do you remember what happened once they finished the job, once they had decanted all the fuel?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I have a vague recollection of the events. When all the jerrycans were full, there was some fuel still left in the barrel, and they were short of jerrycans, and that's how the whole thing ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that some fuel was left in the barrel, are you referring to the quantity that was returned or something else?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the returned quantity. I believe that's what had been left, although they wanted to take that as well. I could not give them the barrel. I had to return the barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, does this mean that the fuel that you returned was returned because they did not have enough jerrycans?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you well, they wanted to take all the fuel in the barrel, together with the barrel. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they wanted to do that but I could not give them the barrel. I had to return all the barrels.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. Did any one of them sign a piece of paper for you confirming the receipt of the fuel? Did they sign for the receipt of the 360 litres of fuel as specified in the log?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: They could not sign this because I did to the have that document on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You're talking about the list that you have on the screen right now?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they provide you with another piece of paper? Did they sign anything else for you, any other document, in confirmation of the receipt of the fuel? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the place where the decanting of the fuel took place, were there any vehicles or a lorry nearby or something of that sort, double parked maybe?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. I did not pay much attention, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When they were left without any jerrycans, did they ask you perhaps to wait until they managed to find some other containers for the rest of the fuel, once you refused to give them the barrel?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No. Even if they -- if they had done that, I would have waited for them to decant the rest of the fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember -- maybe you can consult the document again, in any case you have already seen the vehicle work log. Can you remember when was it that you left for Pilica with the fuel and when did you come back?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: As it says in the work log, I returned at 2130 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You returned at 2130 hours. How long did it take you to get to Pilica? But let me ask you this first: When you were driving the fuel or on the way back, did you make a pit stop? Did you go somewhere else? Did you spend any time doing something else?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you went directly to Pilica from Zvornik, and then you returned directly back to the barracks, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did it take you to travel the distance between your starting point, which was Karakaj, to Pilica?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: 30 to 35 minutes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And was the time the same on the way back?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You have told us how long was your stay over there. But let me ask you this: On that day, did you go to Branjevo at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, did you go to Kula or, rather, to the place near Pilica where the Kula school is? That's also the name of the area. Did you go there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As you were passing through Pilica, did you hear shots or something to that effect or while you were standing in the place where the fuel was being decanted, did you hear any shooting at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since you had passed through Pilica, you know roughly where the culture hall is and the other most important buildings in Pilica. Do you remember whether, on the road or by the road, did you see any dead bodies on the day when you were travelling there or on the way back?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any troops in Pilica, a larger group of soldiers or something to that effect or maybe by the road as you were travelling from Zvornik to the place where you decanted the fuel and then back? Did you see any troops, a larger -- a larger group of soldiers of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I did not see a larger number. I just saw some individuals wearing uniforms, but everybody wore uniforms around those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you hear that in the Pilica culture hall, a group of Muslims had been killed and that the same happened in Branjevo, that another group of Muslims had been killed there? Did you ever hear of that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, not in that day. I heard two or three days later, there were rumours to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know then that it happened on that very day when you were transporting the fuel that we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that you heard but you were not told the exact day when that happened?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you another thing. On that day, in addition to the places that are specified in your vehicle work log, did you go to any other places at all? I asked you about Branjevo, Kula and so on and so forth. Can you remember any places that you might have gone to that are not specified in the vehicle work log?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: There were no such places.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What you enter into your vehicle work log, does -- did somebody in your unit check that? Did they make sure that the drivers really went where they say that they did, that they were not fabricating data? Did somebody control that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Of course. There is no way you could fabricate data. There was no way you could go wherever you wanted to go. You could only go where the vehicle work log sent you to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And somebody checked that. Who was it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: The desk officers, the officials in charge of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I failed to ask you another thing. Among the soldiers, did you recognise anybody? Did you know any of the soldiers by sight or personally? I'm talking about the soldiers that took the fuel over from you.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not know any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You saw them wearing uniforms. Did you see any officers among them? Somebody with a rank?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did somebody introduce themselves to you? Did somebody want to issue any orders to you? Did somebody attempt to order you to leave the barrel behind, when you said that you couldn't do it? Did somebody try to flex their muscles and pretend they were an officer?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: If somebody had done that, I would have taken it for granted that they were an officer, but nobody did. Nobody made that attempt.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember what you did after the return from Pilica on that day, on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived at the barracks, I parked the lorry and I went to bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the document that you have in front of you on the screen, you can see the exact quantity of the fuel that was returned and the quantity is 140 litres. Can you remember when the returned fuel was measured? Was that measured the same day when you returned or maybe later or --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: When I -- since I arrived late, I suppose it must have been done the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing, let me ask you. Although you have already answered, but I want to avoid any misunderstandings. The paper that you see on the screen, would that be something that you would take with you when you go on your trips?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not take this with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that this document is not taken on the trips, this particular one was compiled later, or does this mean that in this particular case, you did not take it? What would be the rule?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, but on that day, I did not have the document on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you present when this document was compiled and filled out?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I was present when I signed for the receipt and when I signed for the fuel that I returned, and this must have been on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you present when some of your desk officers entered the text? Not your signature but the rest of the text that you can see in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you be able to recognise the signature -- the handwriting, who could have been the desk officer who did it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't recognise the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, I'm not quite sure that what the witness is saying is that he doesn't remember that he took this document with him at the time or he's confident he didn't take this document with him at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please answer the Judge's question? Are you sure that on the day you did not have this document on you during the handover of the fuel?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure I did not have it on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw it before it was shown to me by Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's just clarify this. There may have been a misunderstanding here. Do you know when this document was actually compiled, when it was drafted? In other words, you said that it was drafted on the following day. Is there anything that can help you conclude that it was compiled or drafted on the following day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Most probably because of the fuel that I returned, because before I went on the trip, nobody knew whether I would return any or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Do you remember when you were signing the document, if the document had these words in brackets, saying, "For Lieutenant Colonel Popovic"? Do you remember that being there at the time?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I didn't pay attention to that. I only paid attention to the amounts of fuel cited.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get in touch with Lieutenant Colonel Vujadin Popovic at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know him at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't. I don't know him today even.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Except for me and members of my team, did you ever speak about these issues to anyone officially, i.e. investigators, lawyers representing others? Did you ever speak to anyone about the events 13 years ago?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately a month ago, you were informed of the fact that the Prosecution wanted to speak to you. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I received a phone call.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us the following? Did you respond to that invitation? And if you did not, why not?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I did not, because you read to me certain documents which said that the fuel that I had transported was used for killings. Nobody asked me anything further.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was this already at the time when you decided to appear as a witness here? What I mean is did you receive this call from the Prosecution at the time when you had already made up your mind to appear here as a witness?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: How did it come about that you remembered this event? And I mean the event that you've just testified about concerning the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Since this was such a long time ago, I was able to remember on the basis of the two documents that you showed to me. I remembered the fact that I brought back a certain amount of fuel. I remembered having an altercation with the soldiers, who didn't want me to take the fuel that they weren't able to decant back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogicevic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, there is one point which is not clear to me. To my question how the witness was able to remember the thing that -- the fact that he didn't take the document with him at the time, he answered that -- it's line 15 on page 14. "I never saw it before it was shown to me by Mr. Zivanovic." But the witness had said that the signature down at the bottom is his. So if he could clarify that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogicevic, you told us here that you had signed the document that you can see on the screen right now. You also said that you knew that you had done so on the following day. In answer to my question, you said that you saw this document only once I showed it to you. Can you explain this, the fact that you saw the document at the time when you signed it, that it was there? Or did you mean to say that you saw it really for the first time but for the first time after these events transpired?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: When I was signing the document, I only paid attention to the amounts of fuel cited because I wanted to do what I was responsible for. I didn't look at what was written down below.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, when you were signing it, you had the document in front of you, you wouldn't have been able to sign it otherwise?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I merely signed it. I in this way did what I was supposed to do, and I went away.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, this sort of document, is it something that you normally take with you when you have to, for instance, take fuel to Pilica, or is this document something that is drafted subsequently?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: This document was made after the fuel was delivered. I didn't take it along with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Let's now see regarding the other cross-examinations. Mr. Nikolic? Or Mr. Ostojic? Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As we already indicated, we have no questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sarapa, I am informed initially you did not have intention to cross-examine this witness but that now you have changed your mind and you would like about ten minutes. Do you still require the ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. We sought that time yesterday. However, in view of what the witness stated during the examination-in-chief, we have no questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If it's possible, I would prefer to take the break a little bit early and discuss my cross with Mr. McCloskey. I don't think it's going to be too long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. In anticipation of even better news, is the next witness available? He is?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have a 25-minutes break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls. Mr. Bogicevic, Mr. Nicholls, who is appearing for the Prosecution, will be now examining you. And for the record, we have the pleasure of Mr. Bourgon's presence in the courtroom now. Thank you. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Now, let me just clear up a couple things first. You go by the names Branko and Brano; is that right? Because we saw on the materials list for the fuel, P291, that that is filled out as Branko Bogicevic and you signed under that, but on your vehicle log, P295, which you said contained your handwriting, it's the name of the driver is Brano. So you can sometimes be found under both those names; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: My real name is Branko, but everybody calls me Brano.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And is your father's name Milivoje?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where were you living, say, from 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: In Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before the war, let's go back a bit, you said you were a driver. You were a driver for Drinatrans; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And during the war did you ever drive buses for Drinatrans, 1992 to 1995? You did, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I worked for Drinatrans until the month of July 1992. I was mobilised in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as a bus driver for Drinatrans could you just tell us what routes you drove or where you normally drove, what areas you covered?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: You mean while I worked for Drinatrans?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, before July 1992, where did you drive mostly?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I covered the regular routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. What regular routes? I'm just asking where you drove mostly. Through Zvornik, through Bratunac, your home municipalities?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Those were the local lines, Zvornik, Kiseljak, Loznica and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you're very familiar with that area and the roads?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Of course. That's where I grew up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just to make something clear, you talked about how these vehicle logs were filled out on a regular basis and you had to write down where you went and when you came back and that they were accurate, correct? And then I'll ask you some questions about that.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And it's true that when you, as a driver, as a foot soldier, you didn't decide where to transport anything, did you? That was up to the command?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: They told you where to go, when to go, what to bring?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Of course. I couldn't do it of my own will.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And you've testified that you didn't know anything about Vujadin Popovic back in that time period and you don't even know him now, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. But let me talk about some of the people you did know at the Zvornik Brigade logistics unit. You knew Captain Sreten Milosevic, correct? Assistant commander for logistics?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I know him by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you also know him because you worked in logistics and he was assistant commander for logistics, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about his function. I know him as a person by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you know him now as a person?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember when it was that I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you remember who the head of technical services was in July 1995 in the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I only know Radisav Pantic, since he was our immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. What about Milenko Krstic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. But you know he was part of logistics of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Probably, but I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Here is somebody you know, I think, Stevo Gajic.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And what was his job in the Zvornik Brigade in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: He was a rather oldish man, and he was the one who decanted fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He ran the gas station at Karakaj, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Even slept there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you know a man named Milenko Tomic, another driver? Think carefully.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: His family name is familiar. What's his father's name?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you off-hand but he's another driver, drove -- worked for Metalno but he drove for the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Since I know two colleagues of mine and they have the same first and last names, I don't want to make mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But you know a Milenko Tomic who is a colleague of yours?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: There is another individual with the same first and last name but I do know this Tomic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And how were you -- so these are the people that you would have had daily contact with in logistics. What about -- do you know who the commander of the 2nd Battalion was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you know where their headquarters was at that time?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What about the 4th Battalion? Who was commander in July 1995? If you don't know, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Several individuals changed on that position and I don't know who ultimately was commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. What about the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you know where the 1st Battalion headquarters was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you know anybody in the 1st Battalion in July 1995 by sight or as a friend?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know who Slavko Peric is, what his job was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: As a driver?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, I'm just asking if you know what that person's job was in July 1995. If you don't know or don't remember, it's okay. It's not meant to be like a quiz.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Slavko Peric was there, a colleague of mine from the company. He drove a bus from the barracks. Unfortunately he passed away last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you very quickly now about -- let's move back a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could we have P295 up? And we'll need to put the English back on the ELMO. This is pages 11 and 12 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: While that's coming up, let me just confirm that you said you didn't really remember anything about this trip to Pilica or any information about this until your memory was refreshed by the documents that Mr. Zivanovic showed you last year, correct? That was your testimony.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to see if I can maybe help you remember something else. Can you see your vehicle log there in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: This isn't my work log.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It should be page 11. Actually, if I could give the witness the original so he can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't know if my colleague wants to see it first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to see it, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I believe the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So if you want to, you can look at that original there, sir, and if we could go to page 12 now in the B/C/S, that's the next page for you, and it would also be the next page on the ELMO, excuse me. Now, looking down column 4, which is filled out in your handwriting, we come to the 15th of July 1995, which has Standard, then another word, and then Orahova or Orahovo. Now, look at that, see if that helps you remember. I'd like you to tell us about your trip to Orahovac on the 15th of July which apparently took place pretty much the whole day. Where did you go in Orahovac and why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I probably transported food and troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And looking at this, it's 9.00 a.m., it looks like, 2130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, Mr. Nicholls, why don't you ask him to read that column, route.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you read the whole route you took on the 15th of July, please? That's the fifth entry from the bottom, about. Could you read out for Their Honours where you went that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. "Standard, Kitovnice, Orahovac."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, and Kitovnice is the IKM, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And so you get there by driving through Orahovac and then - I've been there - you drive up these kind of dirt, gravel roads into the hills, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: There are asphalt -- there is an asphalted road to Orahovac and a dirt road to Kitovnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's -- thank you. Now, what did you see in the area of the school and just past the school in that big field on the left by the water point that day when you were going to Kitovnice? Try to remember.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember a single thing. I drove without paying attention to anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Hmm. Do you know what happened in Orahovac on the 14th of July? Well, really late at night on the 13th but all day on the 14th and into the night on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember what happened at the Orahovac school? Did you ever hear what happened at the Orahovac school and that field nearby during July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember that all around Zvornik in July 1995, Muslim men were held in schools and then taken out and executed? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Several days later, when the radio and TV stations started broadcasting news about it, that was when I learned about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The reason I ask is that you drove right past the scene of the mass killings at the Orahovac school and the field nearby the day after it happened, while the burials were still going on, so I was wondering if you don't remember that, digging equipment, bodies lying all over the field?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I most definitely did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to move now and ask you -- keep looking at that document; you can look at the one in front of you or the other one -- at the 17th of July, the next day, not the next day from Orahovac but the next day from the trip to Pilica that you discussed. You were on the road from that day from noon to 7.00 p.m., we can see from column 2 and you went back to Pilica. Where did you go that day, first of all, it's a compound question, but then, what were you doing in Pilica? Maybe this will help you remember, looking at that document again.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember what was that I was transporting. I remember going there but not what I was transporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Where exactly did you go?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: As it says here, "Standard, Kruske, Pilica, Zvornik."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where did you go exactly in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And where exactly is Kruske, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: This is a place on the way to Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So the 15th is basically a blank, the 17th is a blank, you've got some recollection about the 16th and we will talk about that in a minute. I'd like to bring 377 up, please. And I -- first of all, I'd like to go to English page 29, B/C/S page 148. I hope that's right. And this should be the version which is 02935619, the complete version, I'm told, of the English. Now, what you're going to see, sir, is the duty officer notebook from the Zvornik Brigade, and since you didn't have any recollection about this trip at all or the times or what happened until you looked at those documents from Mr. Zivanovic, I want to show you this one. Now, first of all, did Mr. Zivanovic show you this document when he met you or when he proofed you? Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Did Mr. Zivanovic show you this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you look -- this is page 148 in the English, Your Honours. The ERN is 02935766.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we have the right document. The one we have in English is 5648.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, page 29 of the English. No. Okay. All right. 148 of the English, I'm sorry. There are different versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what's the ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's the correct ERN number ending in 02935766, 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to read out this entry to you. "At 1400 hours Popovic requested a bus with a full tank and 500 litres of D 2. Zlatar duty officer and Golic informed." Do you know what Zlatar stood for in July 1995, what that was code for?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I was not familiar with all that. I was just a foot soldier, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's Drina Corps command, and I won't go through them with you but I'll just tell you that we have in evidence in this case P1189, an intercept which links to this entry in the duty officer notebook. That intercept is from 16 July at the same time, 1358, and in that intercept, the Zvornik Brigade duty officer calls the Drina Corps command, speaks to Pavo Golic, who is an intelligence deputy, and says that Lieutenant Colonel Popovic needs 500 litres of D 2 fuel immediately and he needs it at Pilica village. And then we have another intercept, 1199, at 1912, that same day, saying that the fuel problem for Zvornik is solved. So now, that's the window from the duty officer notebook, the intercepts talking about the fuel delivery, 2.00 p.m. to 7.00 p.m. Now, that help you remember that it was within that time that you made your trip to Pilica village on 16th of July to deliver that fuel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would just ask my friend to be careful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I just like to tell that it is problem for Zvornik is solved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, he is trying to correct the transcript. Line 20 on page 28 says that same day saying that the fuel problem for Zvornik is solved. That needs to be corrected. Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do not see a point in this question. It is not the same place as --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Exactly my point, Your Honour. That's a submission and it's argument and it's not a proper objection. If he doesn't see the point of my question he can simply correct it on redirect and if he's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Please proceed with your question. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like if the witness could remove his headphones and I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see if he understands English first. Do you understand English? Mr. Bogicevic, do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could I ask you to remove your headphones for a while, please? Now, will you be addressing the Chamber in English or in --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In English, in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This conversation was related to the two tonnes, 2.000 litres of fuel for Zvornik, as far as I know, that's it, not for specifically 500 litres for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think I even need to respond to that. There is a duty officer notebook saying there is a problem with -- that Popovic needs fuel immediately, there is an intercept earlier saying that fuel needs to be delivered immediately, at 2.00 p.m., and that there needs to be 500 litres of D 2 going to Pilica village. There is an intercept at 1712 with Basovic, who is one of the people on the earlier intercept, and he says that Zvornik is solved. I think it's a fair inference that it's the Zvornik Brigade problem of the 500 litres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. This is basically a submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can address if on redirect if you wish to do so, Mr. Zivanovic. In the meantime let's proceed with the question. And it remains a submission at the end of the day because if there is a disagreement amongst you or between you as to which consignment of fuel it refers to, I think we will be in a position to handle it and you will have all the opportunity to make submissions. Mr. Nicholls, if you wish to repeat the question to the witness, please? You need -- Mr. Bogicevic, can you follow now? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Would you like to repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, what I was asking you about, because you'd stated on your direct examination that all of your recollection of the 16th July trip to Pilica when you delivered this fuel was based on documents and your meeting with Mr. Zivanovic and the proofing session and what he showed you. I'm showing you some more things to try to help you remember the time. We see that you were on the road all day basically on the 16th of July, from your log. What I've shown you now is an entry from 1400 in the Zvornik Brigade duty officer notebook saying that Vujadin Popovic needs fuel immediately and -- or his work will stop and that he needs 500 litres. I've shown -- told you about the intercept --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Zivanovic, let him finish the question first.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I've told you about the intercept at the same time saying that 500 litres of D 2 needs to go to Popovic at Pilica village and I've shown you and told you about the intercept at 17 -- at 1912 that same day saying that the fuel problem for Zvornik is solved. Now, that's the window. The notebook, the intercepts, everything shows that this took place between 2.00 p.m. and 7.00 p.m. Now, does that help you remember the time of your trip to Pilica village on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I haven't a clue about these conversations. I don't know anything about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that's not answering the question. The question is the following: Mr. Nicholls has given you this information, which for the time being you need to take exists in the records of this case, and he is asking you whether this helps to jog your memory as to what happened on that particular day, on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So when did you leave for Pilica and when did you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: You can see in the vehicle work log, and I've explained just recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The vehicle work log shows that you were on the road on the 16th of July from 7.00 to 9.30 p.m., 7.00 a.m. to 9.30 p.m. It doesn't say when you arrived at Pilica. I've shown you now that the request for fuel to Pilica came at 2.00 p.m. and that the fuel problem was solved some hours later. When did you bring the fuel to Pilica? If you don't remember, you don't remember. I'm asking if that helps you remember.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see it in the vehicle work log when I returned from Pilica and you can also see -- or so it turns outs that I departed for Pilica at 7.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay, let's bring up the vehicle work log, please. And it's P295, page 12 in the B/C/S, page 2 of the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. We need a clarification here because in your question, if you look at line 8 on page 32, you put to the witness as a time frame 7.00 in the morning to 9.30 in the evening, and he seems to be indicating that from this document, you should or he should or we should be talking of 7.30 in the evening to 9.30 in the evening. There is a great difference between one and the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, and that's why I want to show him the log, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the English needs to go on the ELMO, please, page 2 of the English hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you can see, sir, in your vehicle log, just like virtually every vehicle log, the numbering for times is 24 hours. You don't write 5.00 p.m. in the first line for 2nd July, you write 1700. You don't write 4.00 p.m. for the 3rd of July, you write 1600. And for the morning, for the 3rd of July, you write 800, 8.00 a.m. For the 16th of July we've got 700, which is 7.00 a.m., and 2130 which is 9.30 p.m. There is nothing in here that says you left at 7.00 p.m. Are you -- correct? You were all the road all day that day. You went to Klisa, Pilica, Zvornik, and then Standard.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as my memory serves me, there was just this trip to Pilica, with the fuel, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, Klisa is out to the west of Kozluk, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Klisa is on the road to Sapna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you've told us that these were filled out carefully and that they had to be filled out and it's correct that it goes to Pilica, and you haven't answered my question, which is that this indicates that you were on the road from 7.00 a.m. to 2130 and that you did 112 kilometres. Right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: But that's correct but not only on the road from Zvornik to Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you did not remember anything about this trip, you said, before meeting with Defence counsel and going over the documents they showed you. I'm putting it to you, based on all the other documents that I've told you about, the duty officer notebook I've shown you, you went to Pilica in the afternoon. It was a long time ago, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's possible you were there in the afternoon, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I was only there during the delivery of the fuel. And that could have been after 7.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what is it hat on this fuel log that tells you it was after 7.00 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the -- the vehicle work log, it says I was at the barracks at 2130 so that means that I was in Pilica at the time when it says I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go now -- we'll come back to that -- to P291. Could we get the original? If I could give the witness the original? Now, that's the materials list for the fuel that you brought to Pilica, you testified about that, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Answer so the microphone could hear you.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I want to see if you know some of the other signatures on this document. Right below where it says 500 and also at the bottom under the box just to the right of the stamp, there is a signature. Do you recognise that signature to be Stevo Gajic's?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I do not recognise any of the two signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He told us that was his signature. Look at it again. I don't know how many times you've seen his signature. Does it help you at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with his signature at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you can see the bottom left under the stamp, it's hard to see, do you see there the signature of Sreten Milosevic? He's also confirmed to us that that's his signature.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Again, not familiar with the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if we go up to the top, we see the order date of 16 July 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then we can see in the middle the writing that 140 litres was returned, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's signed there. And then at the bottom again, in box 38 for operator, we see the same signature, Stevo Gajic. So he has signed this document twice, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I know nothing of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You know nothing about it. Well, look at the document.
