utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: The signature is similar but I don't know whose signature it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. When we interviewed Mr. Gajic, he told us it's his signature. If you take that from me, he has signed the document twice, hasn't he? He signed it when it was issued and he signed for the fuel return because he would normally sign when the fuel was returned, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It is possible, but I'm not familiar with the guy's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. If you went out -- forget about this trip to Pilica. If you went out on a trip to deliver fuel and you came back and you returned fuel, the amount of fuel you returned would be signed for, wouldn't it? There would be a receipt, some paper work, to show that some of the fuel had been returned, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: But there is a paper, here you have it. It says that the fuel was indeed returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what I'm asking you, you might not have understood me, is that was the normal practice. Forget about the trip to Pilica. When you went and brought fuel back, it would be signed for because fuel was very, very precious at this time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It was precious, indeed, and it is also true that I returned every last litre of it, and I signed this receipt note.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And the fuel was precious because it was needed for the war and there wasn't enough to go around and we've seen in other documents problems about running out of fuel, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to talk to you again about your trip to Pilica on the 16th. Who sent you on that trip? Who told you you're going to Pilica now? Pantic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Can't remember. Could have been him or his second in command or even the third in command. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who was the second and third in command?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a wrong translation. He didn't say in command, second in command or third in command. He just said a second or third.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's clarify this, not that it makes much difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Actually I'll just withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You don't remember who sent you to deliver this 500 litres of D 2?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just let me do it this way. If it wasn't Pantic, who else would it have been during that time period of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Without speculating, without speculating.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: By that what I mean is who else had the authority in your unit to send you out there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's a better question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sreten Milosevic could have sent you there.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember any names. I don't know the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Look at that receipt in front of you, the materials list, P291, where it's handwritten 1, diesel fuel, fuel issued according to the order of Captain Sreten Milosevic. The assistant commander for logistics could have sent you to deliver fuel to Pilica, couldn't he? Which is exactly what it says on the materials list.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You can't remember who sent you, fine, but Sreten Milosevic, the assistant commander for logistics, could have, he had the authority, he could have sent you on this trip, which according to the document is upon his order?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: He probably could have, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What were your exact instructions of where to go with this 500 litres of precious fuel in Pilica? I mean they didn't tell you to go drive around Pilica with it until you found somebody, right? Where did they tell you to go?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I was told to Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what were you told would happen when you got to Pilica?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, okay. Don't speculate, but if you were ordered to deliver 500 litres of fuel, forget about this trip, aren't you told who to bring it to? Normally?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I was told to Pilica and that's where I was waited by soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I understand you testified that you met soldiers there who you didn't know. My question is normally, if you're doing a delivery of something, especially something very, very expensive and important where you had to account, as you said, for every last litre, aren't you told where to bring it to, like any normal delivery man in any system, bring this to this person, to that person, to this unit?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't told.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So your testimony is that nobody told you who to give this fuel to when you set out? Just kind of go to Pilica with this fuel? That's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I want you to describe the trip when you drove out there for me. Did you see anything unusual on the way, any -- any -- anything stands out in your mind?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Didn't see any combat?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You didn't have an escort to protect you or the fuel?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And so you drive into Pilica, you come in at the south end of the town and head through there, past the dom, to the bridge, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And along the way, what are you doing while you're in the town? Are you just kind of -- I mean, how do you know where to go with the fuel, what to do with the fuel? You're just looking around seeing if anybody is waving their hands saying, "I need fuel"? Describe it to me.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I went past Pilica and at the other end, close to a bridge, there was a group of soldiers. That's where the fuel was decanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My point is, before you got to that bridge, you didn't know where you were going to transfer the fuel or to whom, who you were going to transfer it to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you didn't know any of these soldiers at all, correct, who you transferred the fuel to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you didn't know anybody in the 1st Battalion at that time. You testified to that, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How much -- how big are these drums of fuel? How much D2 is in each drum?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: There were three barrels or drums, I believe, 200 litres each. And probably 500 litres were decanted into these three drums.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And tell me exactly, you spoke about it a little bit on direct, but exactly how this fuel was transferred to the unknown soldiers, if you can.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: They had jerrycans on them, some were plastic, others metal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. And how did you get it out of these barrels? You said with a tube. Did you have a pump or a -- just explain to me.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: They just had a plain hose, rubber hose, which was used to decant the fuel from the drum into the jerrycans.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how many soldiers were there doing this?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Four or five, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what conversation did you have with them?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we have an indication of how big or small these jerrycans were? Because there are various sizes to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, could you please answer His Honour's question? How big were the jerrycans you're putting these in?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. There were various sizes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: M'hm. So it wasn't uniform, just all different kinds of containers that you're transferring this 360 litres of D fuel to at the side of the road with a piece of hose or something?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, what are they doing with these jerrycans? Just -- you haven't described that at all. Stacking them by the road or carrying them into a house, putting them on another vehicle? You didn't talk about seeing any other vehicles. Where is this fuel going?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It was left there. After we had that altercation about the remaining fuel that they didn't have any containers for, I set off on my trip with the intention of returning the fuel, and they stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. So let me just summarise this a minute and see if you agree with me. We've got the order, the material list dated 16 July, 1995, according to the order of Captain Sreten Milosevic, 500 litres of D2 is supposed to go to Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, Drina Corps assistant commander for security. In the duty officer logbook it says that Lieutenant Colonel Popovic needs 500 litres of D2. In the intercept, it says that Lieutenant Colonel Popovic needs 500 litres of D2 right away in Pilica village. You go to Pilica village, you bring 500 litres of D2. And you have no idea, nobody has told you, that it's for a Drina Corps assistant commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about any conversations. I only know that I made the trip and returned the fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And you returned the fuel the next day, 17th? That was your testimony.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's not his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think his answer will clarify that. Let him answer the question. Mr. Bogicevic, if could you answer that question, please? When did you return the fuel, on the 16th or on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 16th at 2130 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And then on -- on the next day you're saying the receipt is signed for the return of the fuel? Is that what happened the next day, you said, because it was late?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that's why Stevo Gajic has signed it twice, right, once on the 16th when the fuel goes out and he signed it again right under where it says for the return, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It was probably done in the course of the day, but I signed it on the following day, that I had duly returned the fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there has been evidence in this case that in the middle of the day on the 16th of July, Lieutenant Colonel Popovic was at the Kula school. Did you go to the Kula school on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you're not sure? Did you go to Branjevo Farm on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: On the 16th of July, around 500 men were murdered in the Pilica dom when you went by. That was in the afternoon, after 4.00 p.m., a few hours after you -- the call came in from Lieutenant Colonel Popovic to have fuel delivered to him there. Do you not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would just like to note for the record, because my friend is asking a question concerning a phone call that came in from Lieutenant Colonel Popovic. Now, if we look in the duty officer's logbook, that's P377 on page 29, nowhere does it say that the call came from a Lieutenant Colonel Popovic. It says Popovic, not Lieutenant Colonel Popovic. That's on page 29, P377.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. What's your comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The phone call comes in at 1400 that Popovic needs 500 litres of D2. The intercept says Lieutenant Colonel Popovic needs D2. You're telling us you're completely unaware about all these killings in Pilica, you were right there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there at that time. And I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: On the 17th of July, you went back to Pilica again, right? That's in your log.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I could show it to you if you want but don't you remember we just looked at it a minute ago? It's page 12 in the B/C/S. This is again P295. We had already talked about this. You went to Pilica again on the 17th of July. Tell me again, what were you doing at Pilica on the 17th of July? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: This probably stands for the transportation of troops, Standard, Kruske, Pilica Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Right, but you have -- you've already said you don't remember anything about these days. Why do you think that's transport of troops?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I was reminded of it through the fact that it was entered into the work log. Other than that, I don't remember anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Although if you'll notice for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The witness clearly said probably. It is page 44, line 6. This probably stands for the transportation of troops. Probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the difference between the use of probably and the phrase, the way Mr. Nicholls phrased it? To me it's the same. It is the same, when he says why do you think the transport of troops? That's because he said probably it was the transport of troops. So please proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you look at your log on that day, the 17th of July when you think you might have been transporting troops, you'll notice that the amount of people carried is 0.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: This was my error in filling this out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Because the speculation of the witness. He already told us that it is probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And unless you have a serious objection, Mr. Zivanovic, please don't interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, when we started off, you didn't remember anything about 16th of July until you were reminded, you don't remember anything about the 15th of July. On the 7 -- other than my refreshing you where you went. On the 17th of July, even though your log indicates that you didn't transport any people, you now recall that you made an error and it should show that you were transporting people that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: This was an error on my part because 25 was entered into the column of tonnes, whereas the truck itself had the carrying capacity of 2.5 tonnes. This was an error on my part. This number should have been entered into the column for individuals, people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Maybe the error was that it was 2.5. In any event, let me tell you what was going on at Pilica that day, see if this helps you remember. First of all, when were you at Pilica on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: It doesn't say that I went directly to Pilica. I went from Standard to Kruske, Pilica, Zvornik. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Try to focus on my question. The question was when were you at Pilica, as in what time?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Don't remember. Well, do you remember that during that day, the bodies which had been murdered, the bodies of the 500, 550 people murdered in the dom the day before, you don't remember seeing anything about; the next day you were there on the 17th, those bodies were taken out of the dom, put on trucks, two trucks, and driven to Branjevo for burial? While you were in Pilica, did you see at the dom, right there in the centre of town, those bodies being loaded on the truck?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We've got evidence in this case, this is at transcript 11326 to 11333, that that took some time, it went on until 1500 hours. The witness who was loading bodies on to trucks thought there was about 550 and he saw two women among the corpses. Now, Milenko Tomic drove one of those trucks with bodies to Branjevo Farm. Are you sure you don't remember what was going on there that day that you were there with your truck?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I definitely don't remember, because I stopped in Pilica only briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you have a drink or a cup of coffee there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: There was none to be had there. Nothing was opened. And I didn't linger there. I only stopped there on the 16th to have the fuel decanted, and then on the 17th, I transported people, and I don't recall at all stopping in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, you just -- I thought you said you did stop there briefly now on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we do have a confusion of -- between the 16th and the 17th here. Which there shouldn't have been because your question at lines 12 to 18 on page 46 was quite clear. I prefer not to put the question myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour, and I'll try to clear that up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. On your vehicle log, you are in Pilica on the 17th. We have established that. You now remember that were you bringing troops there, you think. And I've told you in my question that up until 3 p.m., 1500 hours that day, they were loading the bodies or corpses from the dom and taking them to Branjevo to be buried, all those victims, and I asked you if you remembered any of that and what you were doing there with your truck that day and you said, answer: I definitely don't remember because I stopped in Pilica only briefly. And my question is: I'll wait --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is again misquotation, in the line 12, page 47, you now remember that were you bringing troops there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You think. Well, then you have your --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You have -- sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. My question is, tell me about this brief stop in Pilica on the 17th. What I was asking you is if you went to the cafe which is right across from the dom on your brief stop?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did you do during your brief stop?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I only stopped for the men to disembark the truck, and then I went back immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where? Where did they disembark?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember what time it was now, perhaps since I've told you that the empty -- taking the bodies out of the dom lasted until 3.00 p.m.? Do you now remember what time you got there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, in 1992, you worked for Drinatrans, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: As a bus driver?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the head of Drinatrans at that time, I believe, was Bosko Milic, if I pronounce it right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You were living in Zvornik then?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember driving Muslim civilians away from Zvornik in 1992 in your bus, for exchange, in quotes?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Think carefully. Do you remember taking busloads of Muslim men, women and children from Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm asking him to remember carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He is rephrasing the question, adding more information now. Please, Mr. Zivanovic, it has never been our practice to disallow objections, et cetera, but there is a limit, and continuously interrupting counsel during cross-examination is not exactly what we mean to allow, unless it is necessary. Yes, Mr. Bogicevic, if you could answer that question. To the previous question you said "I don't remember that I did." Now Mr. Nicholls is suggesting to you that you may have transported busloads of Muslim men, women and children from Kozluk in 1992 and that the purpose of such transportation was for exchange. Do you remember transporting Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You had to think about that pretty carefully. I mean, did you ever transport Muslim civilians out of the territory of the RS and you just can't remember if it was Kozluk? We are talking about 1992. During that period of cleansing. Here is another place. Divic. Do you remember taking Muslim civilians from Divic in your Drinatrans bus and then coming back and telling Bosko Milic about it? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me about that. Tell me about taking these Muslim civilians from Divic and taking them away, when you did that, who told you to do that, where you took them, describe it.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: We drove them to Han Pijesak. We returned to Mimica and they went in direction of Tuzla. That's all I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And at this period what had happened and what was happening to all the mosques in Zvornik municipality when you were taking these civilians away from their homes?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You don't remember the mosque being destroyed and blown up?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Later on, it was for all to see, everybody saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the relevance of this last series of questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The question is, Your Honour, to show that this individual, this witness, was taking part in the removal of the population at that time and the mosques being blown up at that particular period is part of the permanence of that removal and I was seeing if the witness was aware that at the time he was taking these civilians away, that their places of worship were being destroyed back home. I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, do you have any re-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please, go ahead. I see Mr. Sarapa wants to intervene. Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can I be allowed to put one question to the witness after the cross-examination by the Prosecution? I initially thought I wouldn't have any questions for him but I do now, after the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you remove your headphones for a while, please? Yes, Mr. Sarapa? And what would your question be? Speak in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: It's regarding that -- the logbook, for the 17th of July. It's a question of the separate 25 and as -- because the witness said if they were soldiers reported on the 17th of July, he remembered that, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please be asked to come closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sarapa, the interpreters are having difficulty hearing you and so have I, although I don't suffer from hearing loss, so if you could approach the microphone and be more specific about what you would like to ask the question -- the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes. I want to ask him, in the duty officer notebook, for the 14th, for the 14th, this is -- it is noticed that 25 soldiers from the 1st Battalion were -- had to go and be deployed in the region Djevanje Kruske. From the 1st Battalion, this is 25 of them. And yes, it was on the page 127. And I want to ask him whether -- whether these 25 people were those who were transferred back on the 17th of July, and this is what he said that he brought back, 25 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Sarapa, could you give me the last four digits of ERN?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: This is ERN 5745. It would have to be the page 127, both in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I thought he said 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What he's suggesting is there is a record of a request for the transportation of 25 soldiers, such request being made on the 14th of July, and he wishes to know whether possibly these were the 25 soldiers that the witness said he may have transported on the 17th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, let's make life easier. Are you prepared, are you willing, to adopt the question that Mr. Sarapa would like to put to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would leave it to Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You would leave it to Mr. Sarapa but that would create a problem for us because it's -- provided you don't consider it as a precedent for the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry, I don't see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't see the obvious connection. I think he may throw that out to the witness and be asking him to speculate. I'd object to using the notebook as leading under these circumstances, and there is nothing apparent here from the testimony or the evidence to connect this to his possible travel on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is obviously nothing to connect it so far. And this is why Mr. Sarapa, I understand, wants to put the question, trying to possibly connect it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could give a proposal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could have a break and I would consult with Mr. Sarapa and eventually put his question in my re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I withdraw any objection to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think we will deal with it. The understanding is, ladies and gentlemen of the Defence, that this should not, and is not meant by us to constitute a precedent. We are allowing it for the time being because we think that if there is doubt, it should be cleared, but for no other reason. Mr. Sarapa, you could put the question to the witness, but first we need to tell him to put on his headphone. Mr. Bogicevic, the gentleman in the back is counsel Sarapa, and he's appearing for General Pandurevic. He would like to put a question to you before Mr. Zivanovic finishes you off with his last barrage of questions on re-examination. Yes, Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for allowing me to put the question to the witness. Can the witness please be shown document number P377, page 127? Could we scroll down to the bottom part of the page? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Mr. Bogicevic, could you please look at the last line? It says here the 1st Infantry Battalion, 1100, 25 soldiers, sent to Kamenica, Djevanje, Rijeka settlement before 1100 hours. This is an entry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I finish reading it to the end, the Djevanje Rijeka settlement, transfer tomorrow SDO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]SDO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him finish the question first, please. Yes, Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: This is an entry made on the 14th of July. Mr. Bogicevic, do you know where Djevanje is or Rijeka settlement, Kruske and that region, are you familiar with the region?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. That was not the question that you wanted to or you told us you wanted to put to the witness. I mean, go straight to the question that you indicated to us, please, and what was your -- why were you standing, Mr. Nicholls? Do you have an objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It was for the date, Your Honour, that he was reading to him but he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please go direct to the question that you told us you wished to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: It says here that 25 soldiers should have been sent into the region. You said that you drove soldiers, on the 17th of July, in response to a Prosecutor's question. Would you allow for the possibility that the 25 soldiers were the ones that are mentioned here, from the 1st Infantry Battalion, that they were the ones that you brought back?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: I thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sarapa. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogicevic, I have very short questions, three. Can you please tell me, the lorry that you drove, the TAM 80 that you used to transport the fuel, what was its fuel tank capacity?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: 40 litres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean its own fuel tank? It could not receive 500 litres?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Another thing, the Prosecutor asked you about some acquaintances of yours and he asked you about some battalions of the Zvornik Brigade. Do you know which battalions was any of your friends assigned to, the 1st, the 2nd or the 3rd?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the last thing I would like to clarify in order to avoid any misunderstandings. On the day when you drove the fuel to Pilica on the 16th of July, do you still adhere to the fact that you did not go to Branjevo, Kula, or to any other place on that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BOGICEVIC
utterances.text: I am 100 per cent sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Thank you. That brings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We don't have any questions from the Bench for you, Mr. Bogicevic, which means that your testimony comes to an end here. I wish to thank you on behalf of the Trial Chamber for having come over to give evidence. And on behalf of everyone I wish you a safe journey back home. You will now receive all the assistance you require from our staff to facilitate your return.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, any documents you wish to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that both of these documents were already tendered but I'll double check it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, other than the revised translation to the portion of P295.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And since that already exists unrevised, I would suggest that you liaise with our staff to make sure what the right numbering should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We'll do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We will follow the previous practice. We had this before and I can't remember exactly what practice we adopted but Madam Registrar can check. Thank you. We'll have a 25-minute break now and please have the next witness ready. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I just like to indicate one mistake, one error in the transcript at page 55, line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Should the witness hear this or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He can. He could hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see what the correction is. For the time being, do you mind taking off your headphones, please? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is page 55, line 9, after the answer of the witness 40 litres, it was my question, "You mean its own fuel tank? It could not receive 500 litres." It is my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- and then follows the answer of the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- "of course not," yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, that needs to be taken care of, lines 9 and 10. Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Okay. You can -- now, Mr. Zivanovic and Mr. Sarapa, Mr. Sarapa, this is also one of your witnesses, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's our joint witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And you are aware of our decision earlier on and your acceptance that he will testify now and that, in other words, as far as you are concerned, you are going to examine him in chief now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To avoid him coming again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And on behalf of the Trial Chamber I would like to welcome you to this Tribunal. You've been summoned as a witness by two of the Defence teams, by Colonel Popovic and by General Pandurevic. Mr. Zivanovic for Colonel Popovic will go first. He will ask you a series of questions and then we proceed from there. But before you start giving evidence, our rules require that you make a solemn declaration to the effect that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking the truth and the whole truth. The text has just been handed to you. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. Please make yourself comfortable. You will be here for the rest of the sitting today and then you will return again tomorrow so that we continue with the various examinations and cross-examinations. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] good afternoon, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Zoran Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us the date and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: 14 October 1943, Valjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about your educational background?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I graduated from the secondary construction school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us a short overview of your professional background and your current profession?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I started working at Glinica-Birac factory in 1975 and I worked there until retirement. I'm currently retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What unit were you attached to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: From 22 March, I was in a JNA unit, and that was in 1992, and then when the JNA withdrew from Bosnia and Herzegovina, I was in the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have a rank?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What rank was that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Major.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you an active serviceman or a reserve major?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a reserve major.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When were you demobilised? Can you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was demobilised on the 30th November 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were a member of the Zvornik Brigade, what was your establishment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At first I was appointed the commander of the 4th Battalion, and immediately after that, when I was removed, I was appointed the deputy commander of the 6th Battalion. After that, I was the commander of the so-called crew forces, and then I was the commander of the reserve battalion which did not have a permanent composition. And then I was with the staff office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since we are interested in the events that took place in July 1995, could you please tell me, at that time what was your establishment position?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was in the staff office at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Who was your superior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, I was subordinated to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the office was part of the staff or another department?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was part of the staff, as a separate unit, a separate part.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any doings with the Chief of Staff at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you subordinated to him as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: To be honest with you, I received orders from the Chief of Staff and from the commander, but in my own personal view, I was subordinated to my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you just briefly describe your duties that you performed in the staff office at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the staff office we mostly printed orders or typed orders, depended on the machine. We received mail and registered it. That would have been part of our general services, dealing with the documentation, receiving and dispatching and distributing documentation that we received.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are we talking about administration work?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, while you were a member of the Zvornik Brigade, did you also perform the duties of the duty officer in the operation centre?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did perform those duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what about the forward command post? Did you perform duty office there as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, and if my memory serves me well, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if one part of your unit, to be more precise, the Zvornik Brigade, participated in operations around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you assigned to be a member of the group that participated in the operation or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was not assigned to go to Srebrenica, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When the army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica, do you remember the situation in Zvornik? Can you describe it for us in the shortest outlines, not maybe on the same day when the army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica but around that time, during the following next days?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know and as far as I can remember, the situation was rather normal in the town of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember what was happening with the Muslim forces that had been in Srebrenica once the Republika Srpska army entered Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim forces that had pulled out from Srebrenica were trying to cross over to their own territory, i.e. the Muslim territory in the direction of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if those forces ever engaged in fighting with the units of the Republika Srpska army or, to be more precise, with that part of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: They did, and it happened at Snagovo. That's where they had their first encounter, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you have a personal engagement in the units of the Zvornik Brigade that were tasked with encountering those Muslim forces that had been withdrawing from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you remember when it was when you first -- when you were first engaged? Do you remember the date? Do you remember the circumstances? Can you describe those in just the briefest outlines for us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the date when the corridor was opened at Baljkovica, on the 13th of July I was given my first task, and that was to take the police to Maricici.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "The police," do you mean the civilian or the military police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the person who gave you that order to take that group to Maricici?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I received the order from the Chief of Staff, Dragan Obrenovic. He first asked me whether I was familiar with the ground and whether I would be able to take that unit there, even in the dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What time of day it was when you received the order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was late in the afternoon -- or actually, it was already dark when I received the order. It was at dusk.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where you were when you received the order from Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I do not recall the exact room but I know that it was in -- on the premises of the brigade command, in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You're talking Karakaj, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you talk to him personally? In other words, did he personally convey the order to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You acted upon the order, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the area to which you were sent in Maricici? How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I spent the night in Maricici. I stayed there in the morning. That's when they sent a vehicle to fetch me and bring me back to the barracks where I received a new order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How did you receive this new order to return to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that I received it via radio communication. That was the only way I could receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that a vehicle was sent to pick you up and bring you back to the barracks, do you remember the vehicle, what kind of vehicle was it? Was it a passenger vehicle, a cargo vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a passenger vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who drove the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't remember who the driver was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When we are talking about that vehicle, who else returned besides you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I and maybe my escort who had escorted me to Maricici, but I'm not sure. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what about the police unit that you had escorted there? Did they remain in Maricici or what? Did they return perhaps?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: When I escorted the unit there, already during the night they were deployed in the Maricici sector, and they stayed in position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did the vehicle take you to exactly, the vehicle that had come to take you back?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you then learn why you had been summoned back from the field mission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Who told you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Chief Obrenovic told me that I had to get ready to go to Snagovo to link up the police units and the units that were already in Snagovo, and that together we should start scouring the terrain towards Velja Glava.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive this order personally from Obrenovic? Did you see him personally? Or was it again via radio or telephone or some other way?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was ordered to me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you roughly pinpoint the time of day when Obrenovic personally ordered you to take that new mission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can only tell you that it was probably between 10.00 and 12.00, to put it roughly, but I wouldn't be able to give you the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say between 10.00 and 12.00, you mean before noon?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, before noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go to that mission that Dragan Obrenovic had given you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you go? Who did you go with?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I went with a group of soldiers. I wouldn't be able to give you their exact number. I went in the direction of Maricici to link up the line from the police in Maricici to the forces in Snagovo. I was supposed to link all of them up and embark on the scouring mission together with all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you first if you remember how you got to that area.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that we went on foot, because there is no other way to go across the area beyond Maricici. I'm not sure whether we had some means of transport to Maricici.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly what the distance between Zvornik, or that's to say the Karakaj barracks, and Maricici?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Five to six kilometres approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what happened upon your arrival in the Maricici area where you were assigned to go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As I was deploying the troops with the intention of linking up the line between Maricici and Snagovo, nothing in particular happened. Things started to happen once we embarked on the scouring mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you just briefly describe what was it that was happening?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As we descended down to the foot of the Velja Glava, we came within earshot of someone, when one of our men said something out loud, an individual responded out of the forest, "Here I am, Chetnik." We realised it wasn't a small group of people. As we passed through the forest I saw a small group of our soldiers and then a couple of minutes later we heard shooting at the police positions in Maricici.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to you and your group that was headed toward Velja Glava? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We lingered in the forest for some 15 to 20 minutes because at that point in time a column of the Muslim army was going past the area. We pulled out toward the old school building at Snagovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As you left the barracks on the mission you were given by Dragan Obrenovic, did you happen to see him again on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him at Snagovo next to the old school building. I saw him and his driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Past 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you speak to him at all, did he tell you anything, during that encounter? Did you tell him anything?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: He asked me what took me so long, and I replied, "Well, it could have so happened that I didn't come at all."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the extent of your conversation with Obrenovic at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That was practically it. We didn't discuss the action itself in detail because at the time one approximately knew how many Muslim soldiers could be found in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you remember or do you know if you discussed prisoners in any way with Obrenovic at the time? Did you provide him with any information on prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Prisoners were not discussed at the time. At that point I was not aware of the prisoners either being there or how many of them were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you did not provide him with any information on prisoners or persons who brought prisoners along, if anybody did, or anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was not able to. At that point, I had not yet come across prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in conversation with Obrenovic when you saw him that day at Snagovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Briefly. I was told to spend the night there, since we did not know what was going to happen next. We parted ways and went to the area where we were billeted next to the new school building. This wasn't that close. I don't know, and I wouldn't be able to tell you, where he went. I went to the building where soldiers and I were billeted and spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were you given an assignment or an order as to what you were supposed to do next on the following day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was told that I should come down to Orahovac with some of the forces that were adjacent to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall who gave you the order to go to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think I received the order over the radio. I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the purpose of your going to Orahovac? Do you recall what the mission was for you and your soldiers connected with your departure for Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The purpose of my going to Orahovac along with some soldiers was to secure some features around Orahovac and to secure the Orahovac-Crni Vrh section of the road. I wasn't supposed to secure the entire section of the roadway. I was only supposed to secure the Orahovac bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, or the day before, did you see a column or traces left by the column?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th, as we set out toward Orahovac, I saw two trails some three metres wide perhaps. I say "perhaps." No grass was left on the ground. It was stamped down as if it had been trodden upon by a herd of oxen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say elephants?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as if, as if a herd of elephants had passed through the area. The grass was otherwise very high, and the trail they left led toward Baljkovica and onwards. I don't know where. But the grass had been flattened. Imagine you have a patch of grass that hadn't been cut for several years and then suddenly it was flattened. That's why I had this idea of a herd of elephants passing there, as if a herd of elephants had been passing across the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we clarify? The spot that you saw, the traces of the column, was that at Orahovac or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That was at Snagovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As you arrived in Orahovac on that day, did you happen to see dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see freshly dug-out earth?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay at Orahovac? Or can you first tell us what time of day it was when you arrived in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived in Orahovac in the morning hours. I wouldn't be able to give you the exact hour. And I stayed there until the 16th, the evening of the 16th, when I went back to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you spent that night in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a private home belonging to an active policeman from Zvornik, close to Nedjo's cafe, if I can put it that way. And it was outside that house that I spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you on your own on the occasion, or was there someone else with you who spent the night in front of that house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The individuals accompanying me, the signalmen, couriers, and others, did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you given an assignment that day or possibly the following day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't receive a single assignment on that day. I received one on the following day, the 16th. The assignment was for me to secure the Orahovac-Crni Vrh road. I was told that 60 soldiers were being deployed my way, to allow me to secure the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the way in which this assignment was conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was radioed to me. The order came from the commander, Vinko Pandurevic. At the time, he ordered that I secure the road and that prisoners, if any were to be taken, should be kept alive at all costs. I asked him, "What do you mean at all costs?" And he replied, "Well, you'll see that for yourself how that should be ensured." And then I realised that he meant that I was supposed to shoot anyone of my soldiers if they happened to kill any prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Orahovac, on the 15th and the 16th, did you see any prisoners at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw four prisoners that one of my groups captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were they Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were they armed or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: One of them had a hunting rifle on him. The other three were not armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Upon seeing the four prisoners, did you do anything? And if so, can you tell us what?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I complied with the service rules, which said that when soldiers are captured, basic information should be received from them, and then they should be forwarded to one's command. This is something that I did. I took a TAM vehicle, a couple of soldiers with me, who escorted these prisoners to the command, and I was subsequently informed that they had been taken there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that they were supposed to be forwarded to your command?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, to Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think we'll have to leave it there for today. Our time is up. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you. Witness, we have a very important rule here that when a witness hasn't finished his or her testimony, you must not, under any circumstances, communicate with anyone or allow anyone to communicate with you to discuss the subject matter of your testimony. So between today and tomorrow, you have to honour this commitment that I have just mentioned to you. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of June, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
